questions.microtopic_name: Cost classification by behaviour — fixed, variable, semi-variable
questions.stem:
Monthly maintenance cost of a plant:

| Month | Output (units) | Cost (₹) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Apr | 6,000 | 2,00,000 |
| May | 4,000 | 1,56,000 |
| Jun | 8,000 | 2,70,000 |
| Jul | 9,000 | 2,66,000 |

Using the high–low method, the estimated cost at 7,500 units is:

steps: High and low ACTIVITY: 9,000 and 4,000 units
explanation.formula_used: b = ΔCost ÷ ΔActivity (high/low activity); a = Cost − b × Activity
explanation.trap: Pick the high and low ACTIVITY months, not the high and low cost months (June is a trap).

source_refs.note: Standard exam pattern (ICAI/ICMAI/standard texts). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

options.error: highest and lowest COST months used instead of activity
options.label: B

options.error: all cost treated as variable at the high-point average
options.label: D

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem:
Consider the following statements:

1. Maintenance of cost records is mandatory for every company registered under the Companies Act, 2013.
2. Financial accounts report on the business as a whole mainly for external users, whereas cost accounts analyse costs by product, process or department for internal use.
3. Notional charges such as interest on owners' capital may be included in cost accounts but are not recorded in financial accounts.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

steps: Statement 1 is wrong: under section 148 the Central Government prescribes cost records only for specified classes of companies (Companies (Cost Records and Audit) Rules, 2014), subject to turnover thresholds.
Statement 2 is the standard scope distinction.
Statement 3 is correct: notional costs (interest on own capital, rent of owned premises) are costing adjustments and cause reconciliation items.
explanation.formula_used: Cost records: s.148 — only notified classes of companies
explanation.trap: 'Every company' is the give-away — cost records apply only to notified industries above thresholds.

source_refs.note: Companies Act, 2013 s.148; Companies (Cost Records and Audit) Rules, 2014 (applicability by industry/turnover).

options.error: treats cost records as universal and misses notional costs
options.label: A

options.error: treats cost records as mandatory for all companies
options.label: C

options.error: overlooks that notional costs belong only in cost accounts
options.label: D

questions.subject: costing
questions.microtopic_name: Equivalent production — FIFO and weighted average
questions.stem:
**Case — Sarayu Chemicals Ltd (fictional), Process II, March**

Materials arrive from Process I at the start; conversion is added evenly. Lost units (normal and abnormal) are treated as 100% complete for both elements; normal loss is assigned no equivalent units. The company uses the **weighted average** method and credits the realisable value of normal loss to the transferred-in (materials) element.

| Item | Units | Conversion stage | Cost (₹) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Opening WIP | 1,000 | 40% | Transferred-in 42,000; conversion 9,200 |
| Received from Process I | 9,000 | | 3,76,500 |
| Conversion costs for March | | | 2,45,800 |
| Transferred to finished stock | 7,400 | | |
| Closing WIP | 1,500 | 60% | |

Normal loss is 10% of units received from Process I during the month; lost units sell at ₹10 each.

**Q.** Equivalent units for conversion cost are:

explanation.formula_used: WA EU = Completed + Abnormal loss (at stage) + Closing WIP × % ; normal loss = 0
explanation.trap: Normal loss carries no equivalent units; abnormal loss does.

source_refs.note: Standard exam pattern (ICAI/ICMAI/standard texts). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

Materials arrive from Process I at the start; conversion is added evenly. Lost units (normal and abnormal) are treated as 100% complete for both elements; normal loss is assigned no equivalent units. The company uses the **weighted average** method and credits the realisable value of normal loss to the transferred-in (materials) element.

| Item | Units | Conversion stage | Cost (₹) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Opening WIP | 1,000 | 40% | Transferred-in 42,000; conversion 9,200 |
| Received from Process I | 9,000 | | 3,76,500 |
| Conversion costs for March | | | 2,45,800 |
| Transferred to finished stock | 7,400 | | |
| Closing WIP | 1,500 | 60% | |

Normal loss is 10% of units received from Process I during the month; lost units sell at ₹10 each.

**Q.** The net amount debited to the Costing Profit and Loss Account in respect of abnormal loss is:

steps: Abnormal loss = 200.0 units × ₹75 = 15,000 (credited to Process II)
Sale of 200.0 lost units × ₹10 = 2,000 credited to Abnormal Loss a/c
explanation.formula_used: Costing P&L charge = Abnormal loss value − Its realisable value
explanation.trap: Process credit is at full cost; only the net hits Costing P&L.
